svg.aria-label: How to write ്: one unbroken stroke · 2 movements
svg.title: Writing ്
svg.desc: 2 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of ് (malayalam), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansMalayalam-Static.ttf. Stroke order after Sachin Nandakumar, Jayasree: Malayalam handwriting, animated stroke by stroke (github.com/sachn1/jayasree, commit e0c9d57, October 2026), js/src/stroke-data.raw.json: the hand-recorded centre-line stroke for ്, drawn alone; "Jayasree" by Sachin Nandakumar, CC BY 4.0 <https://github.com/sachn1/jayasree/blob/e0c9d57dd32031c948da4d5f8432aae3e22c5bba/js/src/stroke-data.raw.json>. Source note on variation: Jayasree records the candrakkala drawn alone as one stroke: it starts at the left tip, dips round the bottom of the cup and rises to the right tip (start upper left, end upper right). This is the sign's own ductus only; where it goes against its carrier stays the compositionSource's claim, and no written order against a carrier is claimed. Jayasree keeps one recorded gesture per pen-down stroke, so one stroke means the recorder did not lift. Only these facts (stroke count, start, order, direction and end) are taken; no recorded coordinate is copied. The stroke data is licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) as "Jayasree" by Sachin Nandakumar, https://github.com/sachn1/jayasree; this record adapts it, and the pen path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Malayalam outline rather than to the recording, which was drawn over the Manjari typeface. One recorder, so confidence is medium.
